proposals: India’s Directorate General of Shipping should issue a circular for Indian-flag ships and Indian operators calling at EU ports setting out, with dates, their separate obligations under MRV, the Sulphur Directive, FuelEU Maritime and the EU ETS, so operators do not mistake a carbon price for a fuel-switching mandate.

The European Commission should publish one consolidated shipping compliance calendar covering the ETS, MRV, FuelEU Maritime, the Sulphur Directive and AFIR, citing the article behind each deadline, so operators and analysts do not have to piece dates together from compliance-advisory reporting.

The European Commission’s Joint Research Centre should publish the criteria and timetable for ranking candidate ports under the Global Maritime Green Corridor initiative, so partner countries know how and when routes and port pairs will be chosen.

The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways should state publicly whether any Indian port has been put forward for the Global Maritime Green Corridor candidate-port study, so Indian ports’ position in the initiative’s design phase is on the record.
